scope: Every guideline value, unit, scenario, document, edition, table, page and WA-status line in src/evidenceline/data/guidelines.json and src/evidenceline/data/fds01_site/soil_criteria.json.
method: Independent of pass A: this pass did not read the other verification pass or the research notes the data files were copied from.
Downloaded each primary source myself on 2026-09-24 (sources list below, with SHA-256 for PDFs) and extracted each PDF page's text with pypdf 6.19.0; HTML pages were reduced to text.

Found each table by searching the extracted text, read the row, the column and the footnotes, and recorded both the PDF page (1-based page index in the file) and the printed page (the number in the running header).

Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space. Extraction artefacts are kept as they are, for example 'NHMRC 201 1' for 'NHMRC 2011' and '1' superscripts run into column headings ('Residential1 A').

Verdict rules: 'confirmed' only when value, unit, scenario, document, table and page all match; any wrong table or page is a 'mismatch' even if the number is right; 'could_not_verify' when the source could not be reached or does not state the point. Notes are judged separately in note_check and do not change the value verdict.
Two en dashes in the WA page quote are written as [dash], because Evidenceline text carries no en or em dashes; no other character in any quote is changed.
The script asserts that every quote is present in the extracted source text and that every value in the data files equals the value read from the source.

sources.title: Australian Drinking Water Guidelines, Part 5 fact sheet: Per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) (NHMRC)
sources.retrieval_note: Downloaded directly on 2026-09-24. The fact sheet heading says '(endorsed 2025)'. The NHMRC news release and review pages timed out, so the month of the update (June 2025) was not confirmed from NHMRC itself in this pass.

observations: NEMP 3.1 Table 4 now labels the 0.07 µg/L (sum of PFOS and PFHxS) and 0.56 µg/L (PFOA) drinking-water values 'For New Zealand only' (footnote b: based on Version 3.8 of NHMRC 2011). guidelines.json attributes those values to NEMP 3.0, where they are the Australian drinking-water values, so the file is correct; the website may want to mention this relabelling when it shows the two editions side by side.

The two drinking-water rules use different page bases: nemp-3.0 gives page 57 as a PDF page, current gives page 49 as a printed page. Both are right as labelled. NEMP 3.0 Table 4 is printed page 48; NEMP 3.1 Table 4 is PDF page 58.

The NHMRC online ADWG page footer reads 'Australian Drinking Water Guidelines 6 2011, v3.9', while NEMP 3.1 calls the 2025 update 'Version 4 (updated 2025)'. guidelines.json names no version number, so nothing in the file is affected.

The code shows the nemp-3.0 note wording to users (core.py and checker.py say 'This rule has no value for PFOS on its own'), and water_criteria() in tidy/criteria.py sets each_member_too to False for the NEMP 3.0 sum. NEMP 3.0 Table 4 footnote a applies 0.07 µg/L to PFOS only, PFHxS only and the sum. For the integrator to decide; this pass changed no code.
The corpus manifest marks NEMP 3.1 as unavailable because DCCEEW timed out. On 2026-09-24 the file downloaded directly when the request carried browser Accept, Accept-Language and Sec-Fetch headers.

The note's second sentence ('This rule has no separate value for PFOS or PFHxS on its own') reads as if PFOS or PFHxS alone is not compared with 0.07 ug/L, which is not what the footnote says.
